name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q01 - Most stable copper(II) complex from stability constants

questiontext.text: Which of the following complexes formed by \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) ions is most stable?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The thermodynamic stability of a coordination complex in solution is measured by its overall stability constant \(K\) (or \(\log K\)) for the formation equilibrium \(\mathrm{M} + n\mathrm{L} \rightleftharpoons [\mathrm{ML}_n]\). A larger value of \(\log K\) indicates a greater concentration of the complex at equilibrium and hence higher thermodynamic stability.

Step 2: Evaluation
Comparing the given \(\log K\) values: for \([\mathrm{Cu(H_2O)_4}]^{2+}\), \(\log K = 8.9\); for \([\mathrm{Cu(NH_3)_4}]^{2+}\), \(\log K = 11.6\); for \([\mathrm{Cu(en)_3}]^{2+}\), \(\log K = 15.4\); and for \([\mathrm{Cu(CN)_4}]^{2-}\), \(\log K = 27.3\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Since the formation of \([\mathrm{Cu(CN)_4}]^{2-}\) has the highest \(\log K\) value (\(27.3\)), the complex \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+} + 4CN^{-} \rightleftharpoons [Cu(CN)_4]^{2-}}\) with \(\log K = 27.3\) is the most stable.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q02 - Order of wavelength absorbed by cobalt(III) complexes

questiontext.text: The colour of the coordination compounds depends on the crystal field splitting. What will be the correct order of absorption of wavelength of light in the visible region, for the complexes, \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}\), \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}\), \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{3+}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to crystal field theory, the energy of light absorbed during a \(d\text{--}d\) transition equals the crystal field splitting energy \(\Delta_o\), which is related to the absorbed wavelength \(\lambda\) by \(\Delta_o = \frac{hc}{\lambda}\). Thus, a stronger ligand produces a larger \(\Delta_o\) and absorbs light of shorter wavelength.

Step 2: Evaluation
From the spectrochemical series, the ligand field strength follows the order \(\mathrm{CN^-} > \mathrm{NH_3} > \mathrm{H_2O}\). Consequently, the crystal field splitting energy \(\Delta_o\) decreases in the order \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-} > [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+} > [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{3+}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Because absorbed wavelength is inversely proportional to \(\Delta_o\), the order of wavelength of light absorbed is \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{3+} > [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+} > [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q03 - Electrolyte type from silver chloride precipitation

questiontext.text: When \(0.1\,\mathrm{mol}\,\mathrm{CoCl}_3(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5\) is treated with excess of \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\), \(0.2\,\mathrm{mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) are obtained. The conductivity of solution will correspond to

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Moles of complex \(\mathrm{CoCl}_3(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5 = 0.1\,\mathrm{mol}\). Moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) precipitated with excess \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3 = 0.2\,\mathrm{mol}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Only counter-ion chloride ions outside the coordination sphere ionise in aqueous solution and precipitate as \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) upon reaction with \(\mathrm{Ag}^+\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Moles of ionisable \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) per mole of complex \(= \frac{0.2\,\mathrm{mol}}{0.1\,\mathrm{mol}} = 2\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Since \(2\,\mathrm{mol}\) of \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) are ionisable per mole of complex, the coordination formula is \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}_2\). In solution, it dissociates as:
\[[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}_2 \longrightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5\mathrm{Cl}]^{2+} + 2\mathrm{Cl}^-\]
This produces \(1\) complex cation and \(2\) chloride anions per formula unit.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The total number of ions is \(3\) in a \(1:2\) cation-to-anion ratio. Therefore, the conductivity corresponds to a \(1:2\) electrolyte.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q04 - Formula of chromium(III) chloride hydrate complex

questiontext.text: When \(1\,\mathrm{mol}\,\mathrm{CrCl}_3\cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) is treated with excess of \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\), \(3\,\mathrm{mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) are obtained. The formula of the complex is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\(1\,\mathrm{mol}\) of \(\mathrm{CrCl}_3\cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) reacts with excess \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\) to yield \(3\,\mathrm{mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 2: Conceptual Principle
Chromium(III) typically exhibits a coordination number of \(6\). Only chloride ions present outside the coordination sphere as counter-ions are ionisable and precipitate as \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
Since \(3\,\mathrm{mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) are formed from \(1\,\mathrm{mol}\) of the compound, all three \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) ions must be outside the coordination sphere. To satisfy the coordination number \(6\) of \(\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}\), all six \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) molecules must be coordinated to \(\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}\) inside the coordination sphere.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The formula of the complex is \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]\mathrm{Cl}_3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q05 - IUPAC name of diamminedichloridoplatinum(II)

questiontext.text: The correct IUPAC name of \(\left[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2\right]\) is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In IUPAC nomenclature of coordination compounds, ligands are named in alphabetical order before the name of the central metal atom, and the oxidation state of the metal is indicated in Roman numerals in parentheses.

Step 2: Evaluation
Let the oxidation state of \(\mathrm{Pt}\) be \(x\). Since \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) is neutral (\(0\)) and each \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) has a charge of \(-1\), we have \(x + 2(0) + 2(-1) = 0 \implies x = +2\). The ligands are \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) (ammine) and \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) (chlorido). Alphabetically, "ammine" comes before "chlorido", with the prefix "di-" for two of each.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Since the complex is neutral, the metal is named platinum followed by (II). The correct IUPAC name is Diamminedichloridoplatinum (II).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q06 - Most stable complex due to chelate effect

questiontext.text: The stabilisation of coordination compounds due to chelation is called the chelate effect. Which of the following is the most stable complex species?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Polydentate ligands coordinate to a central metal ion through two or more donor atoms simultaneously, forming ring structures called chelates. Complexes containing chelate rings exhibit enhanced thermodynamic stability (the chelate effect) compared to similar complexes with monodentate ligands.

Step 2: Evaluation
Among the given complexes, \(\mathrm{CO}\), \(\mathrm{CN}^-\), and \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) are all monodentate ligands, so \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CO})_5]\), \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}\), and \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{3+}\) lack chelate rings. In contrast, the oxalate ion (\(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}\)) is a bidentate chelating ligand that forms three stable five-membered chelate rings with \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) in \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4)_3]^{3-}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Due to the chelate effect, \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4)_3]^{3-}\) is the most stable complex species.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q07 - Complex ion showing geometrical isomerism

questiontext.text: Indicate the complex ion which shows geometrical isomerism.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Geometrical isomerism (cis-trans isomerism) occurs in heteroleptic complexes where ligands can occupy different relative spatial positions around the central metal ion. Octahedral complexes of the type \(\mathrm{MA}_4\mathrm{B}_2\) show cis and trans isomers, whereas \(\mathrm{MA}_6\), \(\mathrm{MA}_5\mathrm{B}\), and \(\mathrm{MA}_3\mathrm{B}\) (square planar) complexes do not show geometrical isomerism.

Step 2: Evaluation
\([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+\) is an octahedral complex of the type \(\mathrm{MA}_4\mathrm{B}_2\). The two \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) ligands can be adjacent to each other (cis isomer, \(90^\circ\) apart) or opposite to each other (trans isomer, \(180^\circ\) apart). The other complexes—\([\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_3\mathrm{Cl}]\) (\(\mathrm{MA}_3\mathrm{B}\)), \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}\) (\(\mathrm{MA}_6\)), and \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_3(\mathrm{NC})]^{3-}\)—do not exhibit geometrical isomerism in this manner.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+\) shows geometrical isomerism.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q08 - Tetrahedral CFSE from octahedral CFSE

questiontext.text: The CFSE for octahedral \(\left[\mathrm{CoCl}_6\right]^{4-}\) is \(18,000~\mathrm{cm}^{-1}\). The CFSE for tetrahedral \(\left[\mathrm{CoCl}_4\right]^{2-}\) will be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Crystal field splitting energy for the octahedral complex \([\mathrm{CoCl}_6]^{4-}\) is \(\Delta_o = 18,000~\mathrm{cm}^{-1}\). Both complexes contain \(\mathrm{Co}^{2+}\) (\(3d^7\)) and \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) ligands.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
For the same metal ion and the same ligands at equal metal-ligand distances, the tetrahedral crystal field splitting parameter \(\Delta_t\) is related to the octahedral parameter \(\Delta_o\) by the standard crystal field factor \(\frac{4}{9}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9}\Delta_o\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting \(\Delta_o = 18,000~\mathrm{cm}^{-1}\):
\[\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9} \times 18,000~\mathrm{cm}^{-1} = 4 \times 2,000~\mathrm{cm}^{-1} = 8,000~\mathrm{cm}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The value \(8,000~\mathrm{cm}^{-1}\) is less than half of \(\Delta_o\), which is physically consistent with tetrahedral splitting. Hence, the CFSE for tetrahedral \([\mathrm{CoCl}_4]^{2-}\) is \(8,000~\mathrm{cm}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q09 - Linkage isomerism in palladium thiocyanato complexes

questiontext.text: Due to the presence of ambidentate ligands coordination compounds show isomerism. Palladium complexes of the type \(\left[\mathrm{Pd}\left(\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\right)_{2}(\mathrm{SCN})_{2}\right]\) and \(\left[\mathrm{Pd}\left(\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\right)_{2}(\mathrm{NCS})_{2}\right]\) are

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ambidentate ligands can coordinate to a central metal ion through two different donor atoms. Complexes that have the same molecular formula and differ only in the atom of the ambidentate ligand attached to the metal are called linkage isomers.

Step 2: Evaluation
The thiocyanate ion (\(\mathrm{SCN}^-\)) is an ambidentate ligand. In \(\left[\mathrm{Pd}\left(\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\right)_{2}(\mathrm{SCN})_{2}\right]\), it binds to palladium through the sulfur atom, whereas in \(\left[\mathrm{Pd}\left(\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\right)_{2}(\mathrm{NCS})_{2}\right]\), it binds through the nitrogen atom.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, these two complexes are linkage isomers.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q10 - Non-isomeric cobalt complexes with different counter ions

questiontext.text: The compounds \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{SO}_{4}\right)\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\right]\mathrm{Br}\) and \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{SO}_{4}\right)\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\right]\mathrm{Cl}\) represent

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Isomers must have the exact same molecular formula (the same number and types of atoms) while differing in structural arrangement or spatial orientation.

Step 2: Evaluation
The compound \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{SO}_{4}\right)\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\right]\mathrm{Br}\) contains a bromide ion (\(\mathrm{Br}^-\)), whereas \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{SO}_{4}\right)\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\right]\mathrm{Cl}\) contains a chloride ion (\(\mathrm{Cl}^-\)). Because their molecular formulas are different, they cannot be isomers of any kind.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, these two compounds represent no isomerism.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q11 - Identifying non-chelating ligand among common ligands

questiontext.text: A chelating agent has two or more than two donor atoms to bind to a single metal ion. Which of the following is not a chelating agent?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A chelating agent is a polydentate (bidentate or higher) ligand that uses two or more donor atoms to bind simultaneously to a single central metal ion, forming a chelate ring. Unidentate (monodentate) ligands bind through only one donor atom at a time and do not form chelate rings.

Step 2: Evaluation
Oxalato (\(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}\)), glycinato (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{NCH}_2\mathrm{COO}^-\)), and ethane-1,2-diamine (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{NCH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{NH}_2\)) are all bidentate chelating ligands. Thiosulphato (\(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-}\)) acts as a unidentate ligand.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, thiosulphato is not a chelating agent.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q12 - Species not expected to act as a ligand

questiontext.text: Which of the following species is not expected to be a ligand?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A ligand acts as a Lewis base by donating at least one lone pair of electrons to a central metal atom or ion to form a coordinate covalent bond.

Step 2: Evaluation
\(\mathrm{NO}\), \(\mathrm{NH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{NH}_2\), and \(\mathrm{CO}\) all possess lone pairs of electrons on their donor atoms (\(\mathrm{N}\) or \(\mathrm{C}\)) and readily act as ligands. In \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\), the nitrogen atom has already donated its lone pair to form a coordinate bond with \(\mathrm{H}^+\), leaving no lone pair available for coordination.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\) is not expected to be a ligand.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q13 - Solvate isomerism between chromium(III) aqua complexes

questiontext.text: What kind of isomerism exists between \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]\mathrm{Cl}_3\) (violet) and \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_5\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}_2\cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) (greyish-green)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Solvate isomerism (also known as hydrate isomerism when water is the solvent) occurs when coordination compounds with the same overall composition differ in whether solvent molecules are directly bonded to the metal ion as ligands or merely present as free solvent molecules in the crystal lattice.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]\mathrm{Cl}_3\), all six water molecules are coordinated to \(\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}\). In \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_5\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}_2\cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), five water molecules are coordinated to \(\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}\) and one is present as water of crystallisation outside the coordination sphere.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the isomerism between these two complexes is solvate isomerism.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q14 - IUPAC name of diamminechloridonitrito-N-platinum(II)

questiontext.text: IUPAC name of \([\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2\mathrm{Cl}(\mathrm{NO}_2)]\) is :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In IUPAC nomenclature of coordination compounds, ligands are listed in alphabetical order (ignoring multiplicative prefixes like "di-"), anionic ligands end in "-o", ambidentate ligands specify the donor atom (such as nitrito-N for \(\mathrm{NO}_2^-\) bound through nitrogen), and neutral complexes use the standard metal name followed by its oxidation state in Roman numerals.

Step 2: Evaluation
Let the oxidation state of \(\mathrm{Pt}\) be \(x\). Since \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) is neutral (\(0\)), \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) is \(-1\), and \(\mathrm{NO}_2^-\) is \(-1\), we get \(x + 2(0) - 1 - 1 = 0 \implies x = +2\). Alphabetically, the ligands are "ammine" (two, so "diammine"), "chlorido", and "nitrito-N".

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct IUPAC name is Diamminechloridonitrito-N-platinum (II).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q15 - Diamagnetic inner orbital octahedral complex ions

questiontext.text: Atomic number of Mn, Fe and Co are 25, 26 and 27 respectively. Which of the following inner orbital octahedral complex ions are diamagnetic?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
An inner orbital octahedral complex uses \((n-1)d^2nsnp^3\) (\(d^2sp^3\)) hybridisation. A complex is diamagnetic when all electrons in its \(d\)-orbitals are paired (zero unpaired electrons).

Step 2: Evaluation
1. In \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}\), \(\mathrm{Co}^{3+}\) has \(3d^6\) configuration. \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) acts as a strong field ligand, pairing all six electrons into \(t_{2g}^6 e_g^0\), leaving \(0\) unpaired electrons (diamagnetic, \(d^2sp^3\)).
2. In \([\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}\), \(\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}\) has \(3d^4\) configuration. With strong field \(\mathrm{CN}^-\), the configuration is \(t_{2g}^4 e_g^0\), leaving \(2\) unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).
3. In \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{4-}\), \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) has \(3d^6\) configuration. With strong field \(\mathrm{CN}^-\), all six electrons pair into \(t_{2g}^6 e_g^0\), leaving \(0\) unpaired electrons (diamagnetic, \(d^2sp^3\)).
4. In \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}\), \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) has \(3d^5\) configuration. With strong field \(\mathrm{CN}^-\), the configuration is \(t_{2g}^5 e_g^0\), leaving \(1\) unpaired electron (paramagnetic).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The inner orbital octahedral complex ions that are diamagnetic are \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}\) and \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{4-}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q16 - Outer orbital octahedral complexes with equal unpaired electrons

questiontext.text: Atomic number of Mn, Fe, Co and Ni are 25, 26 27 and 28 respectively. Which of the following outer orbital octahedral complexes have same number of unpaired electrons?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Outer orbital octahedral complexes (\(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation) are formed with weak field ligands (or when inner \(d\)-orbitals are unavailable), resulting in high-spin configurations where electrons occupy \(t_{2g}\) and \(e_g\) orbitals singly before pairing.

Step 2: Evaluation
1. In \([\mathrm{MnCl}_6]^{3-}\), \(\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}\) (\(3d^4\)) with weak field \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) has configuration \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^1\), giving \(4\) unpaired electrons.
2. In \([\mathrm{FeF}_6]^{3-}\), \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) (\(3d^5\)) with weak field \(\mathrm{F}^-\) has configuration \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^2\), giving \(5\) unpaired electrons.
3. In \([\mathrm{CoF}_6]^{3-}\), \(\mathrm{Co}^{3+}\) (\(3d^6\)) with weak field \(\mathrm{F}^-\) has configuration \(t_{2g}^4 e_g^2\), giving \(4\) unpaired electrons.
4. In \([\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{2+}\), \(\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}\) (\(3d^8\)) has configuration \(t_{2g}^6 e_g^2\), giving \(2\) unpaired electrons.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both \([\mathrm{MnCl}_6]^{3-}\) and \([\mathrm{CoF}_6]^{3-}\) have the same number of unpaired electrons (\(4\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q17 - Hybridisation and magnetic behaviour of hexacyanoferrate(III)

questiontext.text: Which of the following options are correct for \(\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}\right]^{3-}\) complex?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In an octahedral complex, strong field ligands cause electron pairing in the \((n-1)d\) orbitals, leading to \(d^2sp^3\) (inner orbital) hybridisation. Magnetic behaviour depends on the presence of unpaired electrons.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}\), iron is in the \(+3\) oxidation state (\(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\), \(3d^5\)). Because \(\mathrm{CN}^-\) is a strong field ligand, the five \(3d\) electrons pair up as much as possible, leaving two empty \(3d\) orbitals available for \(d^2sp^3\) hybridisation. The \(t_{2g}^5 e_g^0\) configuration still contains one unpaired electron.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}\) exhibits \(d^2sp^3\) hybridisation and is paramagnetic.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q18 - Colour change of aqueous cobalt(II) chloride with HCl

questiontext.text: An aqueous pink solution of cobalt(II) chloride changes to deep blue on addition of excess of HCl. This is because

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In aqueous solution, \(\mathrm{CoCl}_2\) exists as the pink octahedral hexaaquacobalt(II) ion, \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{2+}\). Addition of excess \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) (from \(\mathrm{HCl}\)) shifts the equilibrium to form the deep blue tetrahedral tetrachloridocobaltate(II) ion, \([\mathrm{CoCl}_4]^{2-}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
For the tetrahedral geometry, the crystal field splitting energy \(\Delta_t\) is smaller than the octahedral splitting energy \(\Delta_o\) (\(\Delta_t \approx \frac{4}{9}\Delta_o\)). Consequently, \([\mathrm{CoCl}_4]^{2-}\) absorbs lower-energy (longer-wavelength, red/orange) light compared to \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{2+}\), appearing deep blue.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the colour change occurs because \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{2+}\) is transformed into \([\mathrm{CoCl}_4]^{2-}\), and tetrahedral complexes have smaller crystal field splitting than octahedral complexes.

answer.text: tetrahedral complexes have smaller crystal field splitting than octahedral complexes.
tetrahedral complexes have larger crystal field splitting than octahedral complex.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q19 - Identifying homoleptic coordination complexes

questiontext.text: Which of the following complexes are homoleptic?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Homoleptic complexes are coordination compounds in which the central metal atom or ion is bound to only one kind of donor group (ligand).

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}\), all six ligands are \(\mathrm{NH}_3\). In \(\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]^{2-}\), all four ligands are \(\mathrm{CN}^-\). Conversely, \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}\) and \(\left[\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]\) contain two different types of ligands (\(\mathrm{NH}_3\) and \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\)), making them heteroleptic.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The homoleptic complexes are \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}\) and \(\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]^{2-}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q20 - Identifying heteroleptic coordination complexes

questiontext.text: Which of the following complexes are heteroleptic?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Heteroleptic complexes are coordination compounds in which the central metal atom or ion is bound to more than one kind of donor group (ligand).

Step 2: Evaluation
\(\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}\) and \(\left[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}\right]^{4-}\) each contain only one type of ligand and are homoleptic. On the other hand, \(\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}\) and \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]\) each contain two different ligands (\(\mathrm{NH}_3\) and \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The heteroleptic complexes are \(\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}\) and \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q21 - Identifying optically active coordination compounds

questiontext.text: Identify the optically active compounds from the following :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A coordination compound is optically active if its mirror image is non-superimposable (chiral), which occurs when the molecule lacks a plane of symmetry and a centre of symmetry.

Step 2: Evaluation
1. \(\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{3}\right]^{3+}\) is a tris(bidentate) octahedral complex with no plane or centre of symmetry, so it exists as non-superimposable \(d\) and \(l\) enantiomers (optically active).
2. trans-\(\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}\) possesses planes of symmetry and a centre of symmetry, making it optically inactive.
3. cis-\(\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}\) lacks a plane or centre of symmetry, so it is chiral and optically active.
4. \(\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\mathrm{Cl}\right]\) has multiple planes of symmetry, making it optically inactive.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The optically active compounds are \(\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{3}\right]^{3+}\) and cis-\(\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q22 - Behaviour of ethane-1,2-diamine as a ligand

questiontext.text: Identify the correct statements for the behaviour of ethane-1, 2-diamine as a ligand.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ethane-1,2-diamine (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{N}\text{--}\mathrm{CH}_2\text{--}\mathrm{CH}_2\text{--}\mathrm{NH}_2\), abbreviated as \(\mathrm{en}\)) is an organic molecule containing two amine (\(-\mathrm{NH}_2\)) groups, each with a lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom.

Step 2: Evaluation
Because it carries no net electrical charge, it is a neutral ligand. Because it coordinates to a central metal ion simultaneously through both nitrogen donor atoms, it is a didentate (bidentate) ligand rather than a unidentate ligand. By binding through two donor atoms to the same metal ion, it forms a five-membered ring, making it a chelating ligand.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct statements are that it is a neutral ligand, it is a didentate ligand, and it is a chelating ligand.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q23 - Complexes exhibiting linkage isomerism via ambidentate ligands

questiontext.text: Which of the following complexes show linkage isomerism?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Linkage isomerism occurs in coordination compounds containing ambidentate ligands—ligands capable of coordinating to the central metal atom through either of two different donor atoms.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{NO}_2)\right]^{2+}\), the nitrite ion (\(\mathrm{NO}_2^-\)) is an ambidentate ligand that can bind via nitrogen (\(-\mathrm{NO}_2\)) or oxygen (\(-\mathrm{ONO}\)). In \(\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5\mathrm{SCN}\right]^{2+}\), the thiocyanate ion (\(\mathrm{SCN}^-\)) is an ambidentate ligand that can bind via sulfur (\(-\mathrm{SCN}\)) or nitrogen (\(-\mathrm{NCS}\)). In contrast, \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), \(\mathrm{CO}\), \(\mathrm{en}\), and \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) in the remaining complexes do not act as ambidentate ligands here.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The complexes that show linkage isomerism are \(\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{NO}_2)\right]^{2+}\) and \(\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5\mathrm{SCN}\right]^{2+}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q36 - Matching complex ions with their colours

questiontext.text:
Match the complex ions given in Column I with the colours given in Column II and assign the correct code :

Column I (Complex ion)Column II (Colour)
A. \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{3+}\)1. Violet
B. \([\mathrm{Ti}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}\)2. Green
C. \([\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}\)3. Pale blue
D. \([\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{4}(\mathrm{en})]^{2+}\,(aq)\)4. Yellowish orange
5. Blue

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The colour of a coordination complex depends on the wavelength of visible light absorbed for \(d\text{--}d\) transitions, which is governed by the crystal field splitting energy \(\Delta_o\). As ligand field strength increases, \(\Delta_o\) increases and the absorbed light shifts to shorter wavelengths, changing the complementary observed colour.

Step 2: Evaluation
- \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{3+}\) absorbs blue light and appears yellowish orange, so A matches 4.
- \([\mathrm{Ti}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}\) absorbs blue-green light and appears violet, so B matches 1.
- \([\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}\) appears green, so C matches 2.
- Replacing two \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) ligands with stronger \(\mathrm{en}\) in \([\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{4}(\mathrm{en})]^{2+}\,(aq)\) shifts the colour to pale blue, so D matches 3.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is A (4), B (1), C (2), D (3).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q37 - Matching coordination compounds with central metal atoms

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination compounds given in Column I with the central metal atoms given in Column II and assign the correct code :

Column I (Coordination Compound)Column II (Central metal atom)
A. Chlorophyll1. rhodium
B. Blood pigment2. cobalt
C. Wilkinson catalyst3. calcium
D. Vitamin \(\mathrm{B}_{12}\)4. iron
5. magnesium

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Many biologically important molecules and industrial catalysts are coordination compounds containing specific transition or alkaline earth metal ions at their centres.

Step 2: Evaluation
- Chlorophyll, the green pigment in plants, is a coordination compound of magnesium (\(\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}\)), so A matches 5.
- Haemoglobin (blood pigment) contains iron (\(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\)) in a porphyrin ring, so B matches 4.
- Wilkinson catalyst, \([(\mathrm{Ph}_3\mathrm{P})_3\mathrm{RhCl}]\), is a rhodium complex used for hydrogenation of alkenes, so C matches 1.
- Vitamin \(\mathrm{B}_{12}\) (cyanocobalamin) is a coordination compound of cobalt, so D matches 2.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is A (5), B (4), C (1), D (2).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q38 - Matching complex ions with hybridisation and unpaired electrons

questiontext.text:
Match the complex ions given in Column I with the hybridisation and number of unpaired electrons given in Column II and assign the correct code :

Column I (Complex ion)Column II (Hybridisation, number of unpaired electrons)
A. \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}\)1. \(dsp^2\), 1
B. \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}\)2. \(sp^3d^2\), 5
C. \([\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{2+}\)3. \(d^2sp^3\), 3
D. \([\mathrm{MnF}_{6}]^{4-}\)4. \(sp^3\), 4
5. \(sp^3d^2\), 2

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to valence bond theory, the hybridisation and number of unpaired electrons in a complex ion depend on the coordination number, the \(d\)-electron count of the metal ion, and whether the ligands are strong field or weak field.

Step 2: Evaluation
- In \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}\), \(\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}\) is \(3d^3\). Two \(3d\) orbitals are vacant regardless of ligand strength, giving \(d^2sp^3\) hybridisation and \(3\) unpaired electrons (A matches 3).
- In \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}\), \(\mathrm{Co}^{2+}\) is \(3d^7\). With strong field \(\mathrm{CN}^-\), it adopts square planar \(dsp^2\) hybridisation with \(1\) unpaired electron (B matches 1).
- In \([\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{2+}\), \(\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}\) is \(3d^8\). With coordination number \(6\), it uses outer \(4d\) orbitals for \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation and has \(2\) unpaired electrons (C matches 5).
- In \([\mathrm{MnF}_{6}]^{4-}\), \(\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}\) is \(3d^5\). With weak field \(\mathrm{F}^-\), there is no pairing, giving \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation and \(5\) unpaired electrons (D matches 2).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is A (3), B (1), C (5), D (2).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q39 - Matching complex species with possible isomerism

questiontext.text:
Match the complex species given in Column I with the possible isomerism given in Column II and assign the correct code :

Column I (Complex species)Column II (Isomerism)
A. \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4} \mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}\)1. optical
B. cis-\(\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}\)2. ionisation
C. \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\left(\mathrm{NO}_{2}\right)\right] \mathrm{Cl}_{2}\)3. coordination
D. \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}\right]\)4. geometrical
5. linkage

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Coordination compounds exhibit structural isomerism (ionisation, coordination, linkage) and stereoisomerism (geometrical, optical) depending on their ligand types, counter-ions, and symmetry.

Step 2: Evaluation
- \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}\) is of the \(\mathrm{MA}_4\mathrm{B}_2\) type and shows cis-trans geometrical isomerism (A matches 4).
- cis-\(\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}\) lacks a plane or centre of symmetry and is chiral, showing optical isomerism (B matches 1).
- \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\left(\mathrm{NO}_{2}\right)\right]\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\) can exchange the coordinated \(\mathrm{NO}_2^-\) ion with a counter-ion \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) to form \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\mathrm{Cl}\right]\mathrm{Cl}(\mathrm{NO}_{2})\), showing ionisation isomerism (C matches 2).
- \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}\right]\) consists of both a complex cation and a complex anion that can interchange ligands to give \(\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}\right]\), showing coordination isomerism (D matches 3).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is A (4), B (1), C (2), D (3).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q40 - Matching cobalt compounds with oxidation state of cobalt

questiontext.text:
Match the compounds given in Column I with the oxidation state of cobalt present in it (given in Column II) and assign the correct code.

Column I (Compound)Column II (Oxidation state of Co)
A. \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NCS})(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5]^{2+}\)1. +4
B. \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4} \mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right] \mathrm{SO}_{4}\)2. 0
C. \(\mathrm{Na}_4[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3)_3]\)3. +1
D. \(\left[\mathrm{Co}_{2}(\mathrm{CO})_{8}\right]\)4. +2
5. +3

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The oxidation state of the central metal atom is found by setting the sum of its oxidation state and the charges of all ligands equal to the overall charge of the coordination entity.

Step 2: Evaluation
- For \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NCS})(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5]^{2+}\): \(x + (-1) + 5(0) = +2 \implies x = +3\) (A matches 5).
- For \(\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4} \mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right] \mathrm{SO}_{4}\): \(x + 4(0) + 2(-1) + (-2) = 0 \implies x = +4\) (B matches 1).
- For \(\mathrm{Na}_4[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3)_3]\): \(4(+1) + x + 3(-2) = 0 \implies x = +2\) (C matches 4).
- For \(\left[\mathrm{Co}_{2}(\mathrm{CO})_{8}\right]\): since \(\mathrm{CO}\) is a neutral ligand and the complex is neutral, \(2x + 8(0) = 0 \implies x = 0\) (D matches 2).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is A (5), B (1), C (4), D (2).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q41 - Assertion-Reason on removal of toxic metal ions by chelating ligands

questiontext.text:
Assertion : Toxic metal ions are removed by the chelating ligands.
Reason : Chelate complexes tend to be more stable.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Chelating ligands such as EDTA are widely used in chelation therapy to bind and remove toxic heavy metal ions (e.g., lead, mercury) from biological systems. Thus, the assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
Due to the chelate effect (favourable entropy change upon displacing multiple monodentate ligands), chelate complexes are thermodynamically much more stable than analogous complexes with monodentate ligands. Thus, the reason is true.

Step 3: Check Explanation and Final Conclusion
Because chelate complexes are exceptionally stable, chelating ligands effectively sequester toxic metal ions and prevent them from interacting with biomolecules, enabling their safe excretion. Therefore, both assertion and reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

answer.text: Assertion and reason both are true, reason is correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion and reason both are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q42 - Assertion-Reason on reducing nature of Cr(II) and Fe(II) aqua complexes

questiontext.text:
Assertion : \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]\mathrm{Cl}_2\) and \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]\mathrm{Cl}_2\) are reducing in nature.
Reason : Unpaired electrons are present in their \(d\)-orbitals.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
In \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]\mathrm{Cl}_2\) and \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]\mathrm{Cl}_2\), the metal ions are \(\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}\) (\(3d^4\)) and \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) (\(3d^6\)), both of which readily oxidise to their more stable \(+3\) oxidation states (\(\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}\) with a half-filled \(t_{2g}^3\) level and \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) with a half-filled \(3d^5\) shell). Hence, both complexes are reducing in nature, so the assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
Both \(\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}\) and \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) in these high-spin aqua complexes contain \(4\) unpaired electrons in their \(d\)-orbitals, so the reason is also true.

Step 3: Check Explanation and Final Conclusion
However, the mere presence of unpaired \(d\)-electrons does not cause reducing behaviour; rather, it is the thermodynamic stability of the \(+3\) state relative to the \(+2\) state (reflected in their standard electrode potentials) that makes them reducing agents. Therefore, both assertion and reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

answer.text: Assertion and reason both are true, reason is correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion and reason both are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q43 - Assertion-Reason on linkage isomerism and ambidentate ligands

questiontext.text:
Assertion : Linkage isomerism arises in coordination compounds containing ambidentate ligand.
Reason : Ambidentate ligand has two different donor atoms.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Linkage isomerism is observed in coordination compounds that contain ambidentate ligands such as \(\mathrm{NO}_2^-\) or \(\mathrm{SCN}^-\). Thus, the assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
An ambidentate ligand is a unidentate ligand that possesses two different donor atoms (for example, \(\mathrm{N}\) and \(\mathrm{O}\) in \(\mathrm{NO}_2^-\), or \(\mathrm{S}\) and \(\mathrm{N}\) in \(\mathrm{SCN}^-\)) and can coordinate through either atom. Thus, the reason is true.

Step 3: Check Explanation and Final Conclusion
Because an ambidentate ligand has two different donor atoms, it can attach to the central metal ion in two distinct ways, directly giving rise to linkage isomers. Therefore, both assertion and reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

answer.text: Assertion and reason both are true, reason is correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion and reason both are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q44 - Assertion-Reason on geometrical isomerism in octahedral complexes

questiontext.text:
Assertion : Complexes of \(\mathrm{MX}_6\) and \(\mathrm{MX}_5\mathrm{L}\) type (X and L are unidentate) do not show geometrical isomerism.
Reason : Geometrical isomerism is not shown by complexes of coordination number 6.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
In an octahedral complex of type \(\mathrm{MX}_6\), all six coordination positions are identical. In \(\mathrm{MX}_5\mathrm{L}\), placing the single ligand \(\mathrm{L}\) at any of the six positions yields the exact same spatial arrangement. Therefore, neither \(\mathrm{MX}_6\) nor \(\mathrm{MX}_5\mathrm{L}\) shows geometrical isomerism, and the assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
Complexes with coordination number \(6\) (octahedral) of types such as \(\mathrm{MA}_4\mathrm{B}_2\) (e.g., \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+\)) and \(\mathrm{MA}_3\mathrm{B}_3\) clearly exhibit geometrical isomerism (cis/trans and fac/mer). Thus, the reason is false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the assertion is true and the reason is false.

answer.text: Assertion and reason both are true, reason is correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion and reason both are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MCQ_Q45 - Assertion-Reason on magnetic moment and hybridisation of hexacyanoferrate(III)

questiontext.text:
Assertion : \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}\) ion shows magnetic moment corresponding to two unpaired electrons.
Reason : Because it has \(d^2sp^3\) type hybridisation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
In \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}\), iron is in the \(+3\) oxidation state (\(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\), \(3d^5\)). Because \(\mathrm{CN}^-\) is a strong field ligand, the five \(3d\) electrons pair into the \(t_{2g}\) orbitals as \(t_{2g}^5 e_g^0\), leaving only \(1\) unpaired electron (not \(2\)). Thus, the assertion is false.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
Pairing of the \(3d\) electrons vacates two inner \(3d\) orbitals, allowing \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}\) to undergo \(d^2sp^3\) hybridisation. Thus, the reason is true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the assertion is false and the reason is true.

answer.text: Assertion and reason both are true, reason is correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion and reason both are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
